message.content:
The **United States Declaration of Independence** was signed by **56 delegates** from the thirteen colonies. Here’s the full list of signers, grouped by the colony they represented:

| Colony | Signers |
|--------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, Thomas McKean |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, James Smith, George Taylor, James Wilson, George Ross |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Francis Hopkinson, John Hart, Abraham Clark |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, Joseph Warren, John Adams, Paul Revere, John Hancock (again), John Hancock (again) – *Note: John Hancock’s signature is famously large and bold* |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll of Carrollton (again) |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, Joseph Hewes |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | Richard Henry Lee, Francis Lightfoot Lee, Carter Braxton, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas Jefferson (again) |
| **New York** | Philip Livingston, Francis Lewis, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |

### Quick Highlights

- **Thomas Jefferson** – Principal author of the Declaration and signer from Virginia.
- **John Adams** – Future second President of the United States, signer from Massachusetts.
- **Benjamin Franklin** – Renowned polymath, signer from Pennsylvania.
- **John Hancock** – His large, bold signature on the original document is iconic.
- **George Washington** – Although he was a key figure in the Revolution, he did not sign the Declaration because he was serving as commander-in-chief of the Continental Army at the time.

These 56 men (and one woman, **Abigail Adams**, who wrote a famous letter to her husband John Adams but did not sign the Declaration) formally endorsed the Declaration on **July 4, 1776** (though the signing actually began on August 2, 1776, and continued over the next few months).
